note: For each combination of answers, the rule with the most matching conditions applies. The validator checks that there is always exactly one.

models.name: Mean and standard deviation, or median and interquartile range
models.description: Mean (SD) if the distribution is symmetric, median [IQR] if it is skewed, always with a confidence interval for the main estimate.
assumptions: With repeated measurements, describe each measurement occasion separately.

models.name: Frequencies and proportions with confidence intervals
models.description: Number and percentage for each category, always with the denominator stated.

models.name: Rates per person-time
models.description: Number of events divided by total observation time, for example per 1000 person-years, with a confidence interval.
assumptions: The observation time of each subject must be known.

models.name: Kaplan-Meier curve
models.description: Survival curve with the number at risk below the plot, median survival and survival at fixed clinical time points.
assumptions: Censoring is non-informative: subjects who leave the study have the same risk as those who stay.

models.name: Cumulative incidence (Aalen-Johansen)
models.description: Cumulative incidence of each type of event. One minus Kaplan-Meier overestimates the risk when there are competing events.

models.name: Linear regression
models.description: Estimates the mean difference in the outcome between groups, or per unit of a covariate, adjusted for the other covariates.
models.simpleTest: Welch t-test for 2 groups; Mann-Whitney test if the distribution is very skewed and the sample is small; ANOVA or Kruskal-Wallis for more than 2 groups.

alternatives.name: Splines or fractional polynomials
alternatives.when: Non-linear relationship with a continuous covariate

assumptions: Linear relationship with continuous covariates
Residuals with constant variance
Residuals roughly normal (less important in large samples)

models.name: Linear mixed model
models.description: Linear regression with random effects for the subject or the cluster. It uses all available measurements, even when some subjects have fewer.
models.simpleTest: Paired t-test or Wilcoxon signed-rank test for 2 paired measurements; repeated-measures ANOVA only if no data are missing.

alternatives.name: GEE
alternatives.when: The question is about the population-average effect, not the effect on the individual subject

assumptions: Data missing at random (missingness explained by observed variables)
Appropriate correlation structure

models.name: Logistic regression
models.description: Estimates the adjusted odds ratio. For effects on common outcomes, add the risk ratio estimated with modified Poisson regression.
models.simpleTest: Chi-squared test; Fisher's exact test if any expected count is below 5.

alternatives.name: Modified Poisson (robust standard errors) or log-binomial regression
alternatives.when: Common outcome and the risk ratio is wanted

models.measure: Odds ratio with 95% CI; risk ratio and absolute risks for clinicians
assumptions: Linearity on the logit scale for continuous covariates
Enough events per parameter

models.name: Mixed-effects logistic regression or GEE
models.description: The mixed model estimates an odds ratio conditional on the subject or cluster; GEE estimates a population-average odds ratio.

alternatives.name: GEE
alternatives.when: The question is about the population-average effect

assumptions: Enough clusters to estimate the between-cluster variance

models.name: Ordinal logistic regression (proportional odds)
models.description: Uses the whole order of the categories, without dichotomising the outcome.
models.simpleTest: Mann-Whitney test for 2 groups; Kruskal-Wallis test for more groups.

alternatives.name: Multinomial logistic regression
alternatives.when: The proportional odds assumption is clearly violated

models.measure: Common odds ratio across all cut-points, with 95% CI
assumptions: Proportional odds: the effect is the same at every cut-point of the outcome

models.name: Mixed-effects ordinal model
models.description: Proportional odds model with random effects for the subject or the cluster.
models.simpleTest: Wilcoxon signed-rank test for 2 paired measurements.
assumptions: Proportional odds

models.name: Multinomial logistic regression
models.description: A set of odds ratios for each category against a reference category.
models.measure: Odds ratio per category with 95% CI
assumptions: Many parameters: many events are needed in each category

models.name: Mixed-effects multinomial model
models.description: Multinomial logistic regression with random effects for the subject or the cluster.
models.measure: Odds ratio per category with 95% CI
assumptions: Many parameters: many events are needed in each category

models.name: Poisson regression with an offset
models.description: Estimates the rate ratio. The offset (log of the observation time) accounts for subjects followed for different lengths of time.

alternatives.name: Negative binomial regression
alternatives.when: The variance is much larger than the mean (overdispersion)

alternatives.name: Zero-inflated models
alternatives.when: Many more zeros than the model predicts

assumptions: Variance equal to the mean (Poisson)
Independent events within the same subject

models.name: Mixed-effects Poisson or negative binomial model
models.description: Count model with random effects for the subject or the cluster.

alternatives.name: GEE for counts
alternatives.when: The question is about the population-average effect

assumptions: Check for overdispersion

models.name: Cox model
models.description: Estimates the adjusted hazard ratio. Always show it together with Kaplan-Meier curves.

alternatives.name: Restricted mean survival time (RMST)
alternatives.when: The hazard ratio changes over time, or a more intuitive measure is needed

alternatives.name: Flexible parametric models
alternatives.when: Absolute risk over time is needed, or extrapolation

models.measure: Hazard ratio with 95% CI; for clinicians, absolute risk at a fixed time and RMST
assumptions: Non-informative censoring
Proportional hazards: if they do not hold, report hazard ratios by period or the RMST

models.name: Cox model with frailty or robust standard errors
models.description: Cox model with a random effect (frailty) for the cluster, or with robust standard errors for clustered subjects.
models.simpleTest: Kaplan-Meier curves and stratified log-rank test.
assumptions: Proportional hazards
Non-informative censoring

models.name: Cause-specific Cox model
models.description: For an aetiological question: one Cox model for each type of event, treating competing events as censored. Also report the cumulative incidence.

alternatives.name: Fine-Gray model
alternatives.when: Add it to describe the effect on the absolute risk

models.measure: Cause-specific hazard ratio with 95% CI, for each type of event
assumptions: Proportional hazards for each cause

models.name: Fine-Gray model
models.description: To predict the absolute risk of an event in the presence of competing events. Also report the cause-specific hazards.
models.measure: Subdistribution hazard ratio and predicted cumulative incidence
assumptions: The subdistribution hazard ratio has no simple causal interpretation

models.name: Bland-Altman plot and intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC)
models.description: Bland-Altman for agreement between two methods (mean difference and limits of agreement); ICC for reliability between raters or repetitions.
models.measure: Mean difference and 95% limits of agreement; ICC with 95% CI
assumptions: Do not use Pearson's correlation to measure agreement
State the type of ICC (model, type, definition)

models.name: Cohen's kappa (weighted for ordered categories)
models.description: Agreement between two raters beyond the agreement expected by chance. For ordered categories use weighted kappa.
models.measure: Kappa with 95% CI and raw percentage agreement
assumptions: Kappa depends on the prevalence of the categories: also report raw agreement

models.name: Sensitivity, specificity and ROC curve
models.description: Sensitivity, specificity, predictive values and likelihood ratios against the reference standard; ROC curve and AUC for continuous tests.
models.measure: Sensitivity and specificity with 95% CI; AUC with 95% CI
assumptions: Predictive values depend on the prevalence in the sample
The reference standard must be applied to all subjects
